newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal up 4.9 pct from year ago--AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal up 4.9 pct from year ago--AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight rose 4.9 percent in the week ended April 5 from the same week a year ago, while carloads and ton-miles rose slightly, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.
AAR said intermodal traffic in the week totaled 157,077 trailers and containers in the week compared with 149,747 in the same 1996 week. Intermodal does not include carloads.
Ton-miles rose 0.8 percent to 25.5 billion from 25.3 billion in the year-ago week, while carloads rose only 0.3 percent to 333,898 last week from 332,764 a year ago.
AAR said the biggest carload gains from the year-ago week were in petroleum, up 18.5 percent to 5,825 carloads from 4,914, and in chemicals, up 14.7 percnet to 33,755 from 29,424 last year.

Loadings of pulp, paper and allied products also increased 8.7 percent to 11,834 carloads in the week from 10,883 a year ago, while lumber and wood products totaled 5,696, up 6.9 percent from 5,327 last year.
Grain mill products loadings totaled 9,619, up 3.9 percent from 9,254 a year ago.
But nonmetallic minerals loadings fell 9.6 percent to 8,014 carloads in the April 5 week from 8,863 in the same 1996 week, while coal fell 5.4 percnet to 122,260 carloads from 129,255.
Motor vehicles and equipment loadings were 17,927, down 3.3 percent from 18,546 a year ago, while metallic ores fell 2.6 percent to 17,265 from 17,722.
But grain loadings fell only 0.1 percent in the week to 26,483 from 26,512 a year ago.

In the first 14 weeks of 1997, AAR said intermodal traffic rose 5.4 percent from the same period in 1996. Ton-miles rose 3.8 percent while carloads increased 3.1 percent from the same 1996 period, it said.

AAR also said carloads on Canada's two transcontinental railroads totaled 53,435 in the April 5 week, an 8.1 percent rise from a year ago, while intermodal traffic rose 28.2 percent to 26,201 trailers and containers from the same 1996 week.

In the first 14 weeks of 1997, AAR said U.S. carloads on the Canada railroads totaled 717,915, up 0.7 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic rose 9.3 percent to 331,339 trailers and containers from the year-ago period.

Combined cumulative U.S. rail volume in the United States and Canada in the first 14 weeks of this year totaled 5.41 million carloads, up 2.8 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic rose 5.9 percent to 2.55 million trailers and containers, AAR said.
